title: Comparative transcriptome analysis of osmotic-regulated genes in Chinese mitten crab
author: Junyu Zhou
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v4ve8w6
materials: Total RNA was extracted from gill tissues using TRIzol (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer , s instructions. All samples need to pass through the following three steps before library contamination 1 Nanodrop: Preliminary quantitation 2 Agarose Gel Electrophoresis: tests RNA degradation and potential contamination 3 Agilent 2100: checks RNA integrity and quantitation
constitute more than 50 percent of the read.

steps.title: Acclimate crabs
steps.instruction: Obtain Chinese mitten crabs (body weight 110 ± 5 g) and keep them in a freshwater tank for 1 week, cleaning the tank, oxygenating the water and changing the water daily.

steps.title: Prepare salinity tanks
steps.instruction: Transfer crabs to rectangular glass tanks (80 cm × 40 cm × 40 cm). Prepare two salinity conditions: control (0 ppt) and experimental (25 ppt) by mixing brine with filtered tap water; verify salinity with a hand‑held refractive salinity meter.

steps.title: Set up experimental groups
steps.instruction: Create three parallel replicates for each salinity condition, placing 10 crabs in each replicate (i.e., three replicates × 10 crabs per replicate).

steps.title: Conduct time‑course sampling
steps.instruction: At 0, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96 and 144 h, remove crabs for sampling: take one crab from each replicate for hemolymph collection and three crabs from each experimental group for later tissue harvest.

steps.title: Anesthetize and collect hemolymph
steps.instruction: Place sampled crabs on ice dishes for 15–30 min under freeze anesthesia, then extract hemolymph from the base joint of the third or fourth foot using a 2 mL syringe.

steps.title: Measure serum osmotic pressure
steps.instruction: Determine serum osmotic pressure with a Gonotec OSMOMAT 3000 freezing‑point osmometer.

steps.title: Anesthetize and harvest gills (144 h)
steps.instruction: After 144 h salinity stress, treat six crabs per tank with tricaine methane sulfonate (MS 222) at 200 mg L⁻¹, then immediately dissect posterior gill tissues, pool them, and store at –80 °C for RNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract total RNA and perform QC
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA from frozen gill tissue, assess quality and quantity (QC procedures).

steps.title: Enrich mRNA
steps.instruction: For eukaryotic RNA, enrich mRNA using oligo(dT) beads; (optional for prokaryotic samples) remove rRNA with a specialized kit.

steps.title: Fragment RNA and synthesize first‑strand cDNA
steps.instruction: Fragment the enriched mRNA in fragmentation buffer, then synthesize first‑strand cDNA with random hexamers and reverse transcriptase.

steps.title: Synthesize second‑strand cDNA
steps.instruction: Add Illumina second‑strand synthesis buffer containing dNTPs, RNase H and Escherichia coli DNA polymerase; generate the second strand by nick‑translation.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing library
steps.instruction: Purify the double‑stranded cDNA, perform terminal repair, A‑tailing, ligate sequencing adapters, conduct size selection, and enrich the library by PCR.

steps.title: Quantify and dilute library
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration with a TBS‑380 microfluorometer, dilute to 1 ng µL⁻¹, check insert size on an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer, and determine accurate concentration by qPCR (require library activity > 2 nM).

steps.title: Load libraries onto Illumina HiSeq
steps.instruction: Load the qualified libraries onto a HiSeq instrument according to their activity and the expected data volume.

steps.title: Generate FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Perform base‑calling on the HiSeq run to produce FASTQ files containing read sequences and quality scores.

steps.title: Filter raw reads
steps.instruction: Remove reads with adapter contamination; discard reads containing >10 % uncertain nucleotides (N); discard reads where >50 % of bases have quality <20.

steps.title: Assess GC content
steps.instruction: Evaluate GC content distribution to detect AT/GC separation and ensure sequencing quality (especially for stranded or DGE libraries).

steps.title: Map reads and classify regions
steps.instruction: Align clean reads to the reference genome; classify mapped reads as exonic, intronic or intergenic.

steps.title: Calculate gene expression (FPKM)
steps.instruction: Use HTSeq (union mode) to count reads per gene and compute FPKM values; consider genes expressed if FPKM ≥ 0.1 (or ≥ 1 as a stricter threshold).

steps.title: Evaluate sample correlation
steps.instruction: Compute Pearson correlation coefficients between biological replicates; require R² > 0.8 for acceptable reproducibility.

steps.title: Identify differentially expressed genes
steps.instruction: Perform differential expression analysis on read counts, generate volcano plots, and apply appropriate statistical thresholds.

steps.title: Cluster DEGs
steps.instruction: Cluster genes with similar expression patterns using hierarchical clustering, K‑means or SOM; visualize clusters with heat maps.

steps.title: Create Venn diagram of DEGs
steps.instruction: Draw a Venn diagram to show numbers of uniquely and commonly expressed genes among experimental groups.

steps.title: Conduct GO enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Run GOseq (Wallenius non‑central hyper‑geometric distribution) on the DEGs to identify significantly enriched Gene Ontology terms.

steps.title: Perform KEGG pathway enrichment
steps.instruction: Analyze KEGG pathway enrichment for DEGs; plot the top 20 most significant pathways (or all if fewer than 20) in a scatter diagram showing Rich factor, Q‑value and gene counts.
